name: grasps
status: labels taken from the three reference papers the professor supplied (2026-09-28); the 12-item placeholder of 2026-09-27 is replaced
description: Set A: the static grasp types shown in the professor's three reference papers, each recorded as a held pose over the Ultraleap camera with the bare left hand, mimed in the air (no object) unless an object pass is asked for. Labels are the papers' own terms. p1 = Heumer, Ben Amor, Weber, Jung, 'Grasp Recognition with Uncalibrated Data Gloves - A Comparison of Classification Methods', 2007 (Schlesinger's taxonomy, Figure 1 and Table 1). p2 = de Souza et al., 'Recognizing the grasp intention from human demonstration', Robotics and Autonomous Systems 74 (2015) 108-121 (Table 1 and Fig. 13, ten grasp scenarios). p3 = Cobos et al., 'Human Hand Descriptions and Gesture Recognition for Object Manipulation', Computer Methods in Biomechanics and Biomedical Engineering (2009/2010) (Figure 4, Cutkosky classification, and Figure 5). The 'same_as' field links grasps that are the same hand configuration under another paper's name; they are still recorded separately under each paper's label. The picture to copy for each grasp is on 'grasp sheet.pdf' beside the papers.

items.label: Cylindrical (paper 1, Schlesinger)
items.shape: all four fingers and the thumb wrap around a vertical cylinder, palm on the object, thumb opposing the fingers
items.object: bottle, hammer, flower pot, coffee jug

items.label: Hook (paper 1, Schlesinger)
items.shape: four fingers curled into a hook carrying a handle, thumb straight and out of the way, palm not touching

items.label: Lateral (paper 1, Schlesinger)
items.shape: thumb pad presses a flat thin object against the side of the bent index finger (key grasp)
items.object: floppy disk, key, ID card, CD cover
items.orientation: turn the forearm so the palm and the fingertips face the camera; same fingers, different angle

items.label: Palmar (paper 1, Schlesinger)
items.shape: a small box held between the thumb pad and the pads of the fingers, fingers nearly straight, palm open
items.object: small box, matchbox, tape roller, PDA
items.orientation: turn the forearm so the palm and the fingertips face the camera; same fingers, different angle

items.label: Spherical (paper 1, Schlesinger)
items.shape: fingers and thumb spread around a ball, all fingertips and the palm on the surface
items.object: tennis ball, egg-shaped case, bowl, mouse

items.label: Tip (paper 1, Schlesinger)
items.shape: a small object held between the tips of the thumb and the index finger only, other fingers curled away
items.orientation: turn the forearm so the palm and the fingertips face the camera; same fingers, different angle

items.label: Scenario 1: Power grasp (paper 2)
items.shape: a large cylinder encaged by all fingers and the thumb and grasped firmly, palm on the object

items.label: Scenario 2: Power grasp on a ball (paper 2)
items.shape: a ball encaged by all fingers and the thumb and grasped firmly

items.label: Scenario 3: Power grasp including finger side (paper 2)
items.shape: a box encaged and grasped firmly, with the side of the index finger also on the object

items.label: Scenario 4: Fingertip grasp (paper 2)
items.shape: a small ball held by the fingertips and the thumb tip only, palm clear of the object
items.orientation: turn the forearm so the palm and the fingertips face the camera; same fingers, different angle

items.label: Scenario 5: Fingertip grasp with side support (paper 2)
items.shape: fingertip grasp of a small object with the side of the index finger giving support
items.orientation: turn the forearm so the palm and the fingertips face the camera; same fingers, different angle

items.label: Scenario 6: Tripod grasp (paper 2)
items.shape: a pen held by the thumb tip, the index fingertip and the side of the middle finger
items.orientation: turn the forearm so the palm and the fingertips face the camera; same fingers, different angle

items.label: Scenario 7: Directional power grasp, thumb and finger side (paper 2)
items.shape: a marker wrapped by the fingers like a tool handle, the thumb pressing along the side of the index finger to point it
items.object: marker pen, held like a tool

items.label: Scenario 8: Directional power grasp, thumb and finger tips (paper 2)
items.shape: a glass wrapped by the fingers with the thumb and the fingertips giving the direction

items.label: Scenario 9: Directional power grasp, thumb, finger side and finger tips (paper 2)
items.shape: a screwdriver handle wrapped firmly with the thumb, the side of the index finger and the fingertips all on the handle

items.label: Scenario 10: Power grasp with dexterous ability (paper 2)
items.shape: a spray bottle wrapped by the lower fingers while the thumb and the index fingertip stay free to press the trigger

items.label: Circular power grasp (paper 3, Cutkosky)
items.figure: Figure 4, Power > Circular; Figure 5 a and b
items.shape: the hand wraps a ball with the palm and all fingers, fingers spread around it

items.label: Prismatic power grasp, medium wrap (paper 3, Cutkosky)
items.figure: Figure 4, Power > Prismatic > Medium wrap; Figure 5 c
items.shape: fingers and thumb wrap a handle of medium diameter, thumb closed over the fingers

items.label: Prismatic power grasp, heavy wrap (paper 3, Cutkosky)
items.shape: fingers wrap a large-diameter object with the thumb pressing alongside, a heavier wrap than the medium one

items.label: Circular precision grasp, thumb and 4 fingers (paper 3, Cutkosky)
items.shape: a disk held by the thumb pad and the pads of all four fingers, palm not touching
items.orientation: turn the forearm so the palm and the fingertips face the camera; same fingers, different angle

items.label: Circular precision grasp, thumb and 2 fingers (paper 3, Cutkosky)
items.shape: a small round object held by the thumb, index and middle fingertips (tripod)
items.orientation: turn the forearm so the palm and the fingertips face the camera; same fingers, different angle

items.label: Circular precision grasp, thumb and 1 finger (paper 3, Cutkosky)
items.figure: Figure 4, Precision > Circular > Thumb 1 finger; Figure 5 d
items.shape: a coin held between the thumb tip and the index fingertip
items.orientation: turn the forearm so the palm and the fingertips face the camera; same fingers, different angle

items.label: Prismatic precision grasp (paper 3, Cutkosky)
items.shape: a pen held along the fingers by the thumb pad and the pads of the index and middle fingers, as for writing
items.orientation: turn the forearm so the palm and the fingertips face the camera; same fingers, different angle
